game: WAS@KC Week 8 2025, kickoff 2025-10-27 20:15 ET, outdoors, KC -10.5, total 48.5

script.base: Market script is KC 29.5, WAS 19.0. With Jayden Daniels out, WAS loses the 24 carries and 128 rush yards he had in weeks 5-7 and is the likelier team to trail. KC leads by halftime; Mahomes uses Travis Kelce (18 targets, 193 yards in those three weeks) in the middle to build the lead, then Isiah Pacheco (34 carries, 144 yards) runs the clock in a moderate-pace, two-score game rather than a shootout.
script.flip1: KC is up three scores by halftime. Starters sit. Kelce's routes die before 54.5 and Kareem Hunt (17 carries, 90 yards in weeks 5-7; last two rush games 23 and 18) vultures the late carries so Pacheco stalls under 36.5. WAS abandons the run.
script.flip2: The WAS backup keeps it one score into the fourth. KC cannot just run, so the Pacheco carry spike never comes. Kelce can still clear on extra dropbacks. An outdoor efficiency slog (forecast not in the pack) would knock both overs if the 29.5/19.0 script collapses.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not inactives: Jayden Daniels (WAS QB, hamstring) Out removes the dual-threat engine; no backup QB is named in the pack, so do not assign his 8 carries a game to a named passer. Carry funnel, if any, goes to Jacory Croskey-Merritt (44 carries, 205 yards in weeks 5-7) or Chris Rodriguez (8 carries, 19 yards), but a negative script can erase that. Colson Yankoff (WAS TE) Out is depth; Zach Ertz keeps the TE role (14 targets, 80 yards). Daron Payne (WAS DT, toe) Questionable: if he sits, Pacheco/Hunt see a softer interior; if he plays, the 4.62 YPC WAS run defense is unchanged. Matt Gay Out is irrelevant to these markets. KC G Trey Smith Doubtful (back) and T Josh Simmons Out (personal) are the offensive-line hit: pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws. That hurts Pacheco yards per carry and deep shots (Xavier Worthy 205 air yards, Marquise Brown 188, Tyquan Thornton not in the week 5-7 target leaders) and helps Kelce and checkdowns. Sources: pack injury report plus week 5-7 usage.

That pressure path still feeds short throws, not deep shots.
matchup.bleeds: WAS pass defense, 7 games: YPA left 8.0 (82), middle 9.29 (34), right 8.33 (98); 22 passes of 20+ for 233 yards. Rush YPC allowed 4.62, 22 runs of 10+. KC pass defense is tighter: left 6.08 (86), middle 7.77 (26), right 6.81 (81); only 16 passes of 20+ for 208 yards. KC rush YPC allowed 4.72, 20 runs of 10+. WAS middle and explosives are the bleed; KC does not give up explosives.
matchup.overlap: Kelce is KC's top target and the middle is WAS's worst zone (9.29 YPA). That is the core overlap, and the injured KC line pushes Mahomes toward that same quick middle. WAS's top options (Deebo Samuel 16 targets/111 yards/128 air; Ertz 14/80/119; Jaylin Lane 10/113/166 air) do not attack a KC explosive leak, because KC has not been giving up 20+ passes.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both lost. KC led 24-6 at halftime, Kelce was done after three quarters at 4 catches for 41, and Hunt took the fourth-quarter carries while Pacheco finished 12 for 29 behind a line missing Smith and Simmons. The other way it lost: WAS stayed close, Mahomes threw 40 times, Pacheco never got the clock-killing carries, and WAS sat on Kelce so Brown or Worthy took the explosives this defense allows (22 passes of 20+). That counter is strong enough to keep both at lean and to refuse any parlay that needs a 30-point laugher and a competitive game at the same time. It is not stronger than the base read, so the legs stay flagged rather than dropped.
slip_story: One story only: KC control, comfortable not a laugher. Kelce recyds over is the scoring-drive chain mover; Pacheco rushyds over is the late clock piece. They win together only if the lead lands around the 10.5 number and both play into the fourth. Do not add WAS overs, a game under, or Croskey-Merritt over; those need the opposite script. No TDs, one market per player, no depth-receiver legs (Lane, Moore, Thornton, Rodriguez left off).
